findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant-scoped document lookup
findings.body: When document IDs are tenant-scoped, `getDocument` now ignores `ctx.tenantId` and queries only by `documentId`. This can return another tenant’s document and prevents use of the prior compound predicate. Removing the parameter also breaks external callers of the exported three-argument `loadDocument` contract.

findings.title: [P1] Preserve the exported cache module
findings.body: Deleting `src/cache.ts` removes the exported `readCached` API. Existing consumers importing this module will fail module resolution or compilation, contrary to the stated goal of preserving contracts.

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant-scoped document lookup
findings.body:
When two tenants share a document ID—or a caller supplies another tenant’s ID—`getDocument` now queries only by `documentId`, allowing the wrong tenant’s document to be returned. The changed exported signature also breaks existing `loadDocument(db, tenantId, documentId)` callers.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Preserve the exported cache module
findings.body:
Deleting `src/cache.ts` removes the existing `readCached` API. Any consumer importing that module now fails compilation/module resolution instead of parsing cached payloads.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant scoping when loading documents
findings.body:
In a shared multi-tenant database, any caller who supplies another tenant’s document ID can retrieve that document because the query no longer constrains `tenantId`; the authenticated `ctx.tenantId` is ignored, creating a cross-tenant authorization bypass and data disclosure.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the tenant predicate to prevent cross-tenant query fan-out
findings.body:
In multi-tenant stores where document IDs are tenant-scoped, `find({ documentId })` matches one record per tenant rather than one tenant’s record. Query result size, I/O, and memory now grow with tenant count; compound tenant/document indexes may also become unusable.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
